sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2015. Ethnologue, 18th ed., entry Bumang [bvp] (Internet Archive copy 2015-09-22).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No typology line at all; population 200 (Jie 2007), classification Palaungic > Waic > Bulang.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh) 布芒语 and (en) Bumang language, accessed 2026-09-17 (summaries of Dao Jie 2006/2007, Edmondson 2010).
sources.note: Describe Bumang as tonal (8 tone classes / 6 values, examples ka55 'fish', ka24 'door'.. kap21 'duck'), no onset clusters, codas -p -t -k -m -n -ŋ; nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Tạ Quang Tùng. 2021. A phonology and lexicon of Khang in Vietnam. JSEALS 14.2: i-xxix. hdl:10524/52487.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Khang (Nam Mu variety) phonological word (C1ə̌/ǎ).C2(C3)V(C4)T, 99.45% monosyllabic, presyllables with reduced ə̌/ǎ, 'complex tonal system'; Bumang appears only in a comparative lexical table.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-048 (create [bvp] Bumang), with requester form by Eric Johnson / SIL East Asia Group. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; names, location (Manzhang Shangzhai/Xiazhai, Mengla, Jinping), 200-300 speakers, Palaungic affiliation per Dao Jie; sole source cited is Dao Jie 2007.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2010. The Kháng language of Vietnam in comparison to Ksingmul (Xinh-mun). In K. A. McElhanon & G. Reesink (eds.), A Mosaic of languages and cultures: studies celebrating the career of Karl J. Franklin (SIL e-Books 19), 138-154. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Uses Dao Jie's Bumang data second-hand: p.144 fn.6 Bumang 'differs only a little from my Kháng data'; p.144 Kháng word structure 'shows only vestiges of the original sesquisyllabic pattern' with six tones; §3 'Kháng/Bumang syllables and tone' p.150: six tones, low tones 21 and 12 rarer in Kháng than in Bumang; Bumang has no onset clusters.

sources.citation: Hammarström et al. Glottolog 5.x, languoid buma1247 Bumang (Bookkeeping).
sources.note: Nothing; comment: bvp is 'a recent off-shoot of Kháng [kjm] in Vietnam and easily count as the same language'; only refs are the ISO change request and Dao Jie 2007.

sources.citation: 刀洁 Dao Jie. 2006. 布芒语概况 [Overview of the Bumang language]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2006(2): 63-80.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only journal-length description of Bumang; standard Minzu Yuwen 概况 format with a 语音 section (initials, finals, tones, syllable structure) where any remark on 轻重音/weak syllables would sit. Free full-text PDF on NCPSSD (article id 21726343) but requires a (free) account login; CNKI copy paywalled.

sources.note: English-language discussion of Khang/Bumang placement using Dao Jie's data; possible brief typological characterisation (tone, sesquisyllables).

sources.note: The full monograph (phonology, lexicon, grammar) on which all later mentions (ISO request, Ethnologue, Edmondson 2010, Sidwell 2015) depend; its phonology chapter is the authoritative place for any stress / syllable-prominence statement and would supersede the 2006 sketch.
